messages:
Marissa Cole: Trying to lock PRD scope for Dedicated staged rollouts beta. Main open question: which gates are *required* vs “advanced config”. Also need crisp customer-facing messaging (esp for Dedicated customers who have been burned).

Marissa Cole: Proposed beta: limited set of gates w/ sane defaults. Advanced gate editor stays hidden behind “Operator mode” or maybe just not in v1. Thoughts?

Paula Mendes: +1 to defaults-first. If we expose a full gate DSL in beta we’ll spend all our time on edge cases + support.

Paula Mendes: For “required for beta” I’d argue:
- p95 latency (per route/model on the pool)
- 5xx rate
- timeout rate
- queue depth (or queue wait p95)

Paula Mendes: GPU util is useful but noisy / can be a trailing indicator. I’d put it as “informational” in beta unless SRE says otherwise.

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated-specific concern: queue depth is the customer pain. A bad config saturates the reserved pool and everything queues.

Lauren Bishop: I want queue depth/queue wait as required gate + a hard “stop-the-line” behavior. If metrics are missing/late -> pause. No auto-advance.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. We should be conservative and predictable. For beta gates, the ones that correlate with customer-visible impact:
1) timeouts
2) 5xx
3) p95 latency
4) queue wait / depth

Sean Gallagher: GPU util as secondary. It’s helpful for diagnosing why we paused, but I don’t want it blocking advancement unless we’re super careful about normalization (model size differences, batch config, etc).

Allison Grant: +1. Also please don’t ship 6 different “util” metrics as gate types in beta. We’ll drown in false positives.

Allison Grant: If we do include a utilization gate at all, make it one clearly-defined metric (e.g., pool_sm_util_avg over 10m) with a recommended threshold + lots of caveats.

Kenji Nakamura: UX angle: defaults-first reads way better. We can message as “safety rails” vs “build your own gating pipeline”.

Kenji Nakamura: Suggest Console copy:
- “Default safety gates” (Latency, Errors, Queueing)
- “Advanced gates (coming soon)”

Kenji Nakamura: If we do allow editing, keep it constrained: thresholds + evaluation window only. Not freeform queries.

Marissa Cole: That’s helpful. So: beta = fixed gate types, editable thresholds/windows, but no custom metric queries.

Paula Mendes: Yup. And we should specify what’s customizable:
- evaluation window (e.g., 10m / 30m)
- min sample size
- threshold value
- behavior on failure: pause vs rollback

Paula Mendes: But I’d even keep “pause vs rollback” operator-only in beta. Most customers will want pause + manual review.

Dev Patel: Support POV: please default to PAUSE. Auto rollback is scary if it flaps due to metrics freshness. If we auto rollback, support will get paged a lot.

Dev Patel: Also we need a simple explanation to customers for “why did it pause?” If it’s “missing metrics” they’ll freak. We should message “insufficient signal” and point to the telemetry status panel.

Allison Grant: +1000 to calling out metrics freshness. We should include as part of the gate evaluation:
- “metrics delay within X mins” check
- if delay > X => hold (not fail)

Allison Grant: Otherwise we’ll ‘fail’ a healthy stage because Prom scrape was behind.

Sean Gallagher: Careful: “hold vs fail” distinction matters for pager noise. If it’s missing metrics, it’s a rollout health issue, not necessarily customer impact.

Sean Gallagher: For beta I’d like:
- Gate result states: PASS / FAIL / NO_DATA
- Stage behavior: NO_DATA => hold + alert evaluator health (not pool health)

Lauren Bishop: +1. Dedicated customers will ask “is my pool broken?”. We need messaging that separates “rollout paused because we’re being safe” vs “your deployment is bad”.

Rachel Kim: Customer messaging request: can we explicitly say “beta is operator-assisted”? A couple enterprise folks already asked if they’ll self-serve.

Rachel Kim: I’d like a sentence like: “During beta, Redwood operators will configure and monitor staged rollouts with you; self-serve controls will be expanded post-GA.”

Marissa Cole: Yep. PRD currently says enterprise opt-in + operator-led. I’ll make it more explicit in the “Beta” section + release notes.

Paula Mendes: Also: do we need a “quality gate” mention? Even if non-goal, customers ask.

Sean Gallagher: Please don’t promise it. Maybe say “optional / where available” and keep it out of the default gates list.

Kenji Nakamura: Copy suggestion:
- “Quality signals (optional): available for select workloads where evals are configured.”
- But keep it visually separate so it doesn’t read like a standard control.

Marissa Cole: OK. Summarizing decisions for PRD scope:
1) Required gates for beta: p95 latency, 5xx, timeout rate, queue depth/queue wait
2) GPU util = informational (dashboard), not a blocking gate by default
3) No custom metric queries in beta; allow editing thresholds + windows only
4) Default behavior on gate failure: PAUSE + manual approval to continue; rollback is operator-only and not default
5) Missing/late metrics => HOLD (NO_DATA) and alert evaluator/telemetry health
6) Customer messaging: operator-assisted beta; self-serve later; quality gating optional/limited

Marissa Cole: Anyone object? If not I’ll update PRD + send for SRE + CS review.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: Works for me. Put in PRD that thresholds are “recommended defaults” and SRE sign-off required to change defaults.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: Add a note that we’ll publish a “default gates + rationale” page so customers don’t feel it’s arbitrary.

Rachel Kim: :thumbsup: I’ll draft a short customer-facing blurb for beta kickoff emails based on this.

Dev Patel: :+1: please include escalation path in beta messaging (Support vs oncall). We’ll get “my rollout paused” tickets.

Paula Mendes: No objections. I’ll add an “advanced config (post-beta)” section so we have a place to park requests (util gates, custom queries, per-region sub-gates, etc).

Marissa Cole: Great. Action items:
- Marissa: update PRD scope + defaults vs advanced + messaging language
- Paula: add post-beta advanced config section + confirm gate type definitions
- Rachel: beta customer email copy draft
- Sean/Allison: sanity check default thresholds + NO_DATA hold behavior

Marissa Cole: Will share updated PRD in this channel later today.
